entities.summary: Lucius Fufidius Pollio (b. 150 CE) was a Roman civil administrator and military commander active in the Roman Empire during the Late Antiquity period. As a public servant, he played a crucial role in the governance of the Roman provinces in Africa and Asia. His military campaigns took place in the Roman provinces of Mauretania and Syria, where he demonstrated his leadership skills in the face of various challenges. His contributions to the Roman military were recognized by his contemporaries, who praised his strategic thinking and bravery. As a testament to his legacy, Lucius Fufidius Pollio is remembered as one of the most influential Roman military commanders of his time. His legacy continues to inspire historians and military strategists alike, who study his campaigns and tactics to better understand the art of war in the ancient world. The inscription on his tombstone, which has been lost to time, is believed to have read: 'Fufidius Pollio, son of Marcus, governor of Africa, conqueror of the Mauretani'.
